answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation with a slow trust spiral: a new agent locks a refundable deposit and must complete small verifiable jobs checked by established peers before larger paid work. Success raises its limit; failure slashes the deposit and leaves an umber stain on its record that a fresh name cannot erase, since it restarts at the bottom. An attacker must fund a deposit per fake identity and pay the time cost of climbing, while voting weight follows earned reputation, not headcount — a plume of cheap copies adds volume but no weight.
